$comment: USD per million tokens. Anthropic figures from platform.claude.com pricing (cached 2026-08; sonnet-5 is the standard sticker, not the intro discount). Each row names its PROVIDER, because llm_usage attributes spend per provider and two providers can ship similarly-named models. The margin math reads this table — keep it current when a provider reprices or when NARRATE_MODEL/COMPOSE_MODEL/EVAL_MODEL change. An unknown model prices at the fallback, which is deliberately the most expensive row so cost is never silently undercounted; a new provider's models therefore OVERSTATE spend until their real rates are added here, which is the safe direction to be wrong in.
$openai: OpenAI rows from developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing (fetched 2026-08-07). Only the tiers worth setting EVAL_MODEL to are listed — the full catalogue is ~36 models and most would only rot here. Anything unlisted still prices at the fallback, which overstates rather than undercounts.
$fallback_note: The fallback must stay at least as expensive as every row above it, or an unpriced model would silently undercount — the one direction this table must never be wrong in. Raised to 30/180 when OpenAI rows landed, because their mid tiers already exceed the old 10/50. Caveat worth knowing: OpenAI's pro and o1 tiers run several times higher again (o1-pro is 150/600). Nothing should point EVAL_MODEL at one, but if anything ever does, price it here first.
$estimates: Rows marked estimated:true were entered from published rates without a live check against the provider's billing, and every one is ROUNDED UP from the figure believed to be real. That direction is not a style choice: an estimate BELOW the true price is a spend ceiling that fails to stop, which is the one arithmetic error this product cannot make. They are still far below the fallback, so the agents on them are usable rather than priced out of a conversation's ceiling in three turns. Replace a row with a verified figure and drop the flag.
